candidates.change_summary: Remove the condition that msg.sender must be a curated pool, allowing any caller to mint synthetic tokens and alter LP balance tracking.
Delete the line that increments mapSynth_LPDebt, causing the debt tracking to be zero while LP balance increases, changing the ratio.
Delete the line that increments mapSynth_LPBalance, so LP balance is not updated while debt is, causing a divergence.
Replace mapSynth_LPBalance[msg.sender] with mapSynth_LPBalance[member] when adding LP units, storing balance under a different key.
Replace += lpUnits with += amount so LP balance tracks the synthetic amount instead of actual LP units added.
Replace += amount with += lpUnits for debt tracking, so debt increases by LP units instead of synthetic amount, changing the stored ratio.
Delete the call to _getAddedLPAmount, causing lpUnits to be zero and thus mapSynth_LPBalance unchanged.
Replace msg.sender with member in the onlyPool modifier invocation, allowing the member address to be passed as the pool.
Delete the increment of mapSynth_LPBalance[msg.sender], so mintSynth no longer records the caller's LP balance delta.
Delete the onlyPool modifier invocation on mintSynth, allowing any caller to mint synth and thereby modify mapSynth_LPBalance for that caller.
Delete the onlyPool guard's require, allowing any caller to invoke mintSynth and update mapSynth_LPDebt.
Delete the accounting update that increases mapSynth_LPDebt for the caller, so the debt mapping is no longer updated.
Replace mapSynth_LPDebt[msg.sender] += amount with -= amount, reversing the debt accounting observable at the caller's key.
Move the mapSynth_LPDebt update after the external _mint call, changing the debt visible during reentrancy.
Update mapSynth_LPDebt for the member argument instead of msg.sender, changing which key's debt is observed.

Replace the _transfer call with a direct self-transfer of the unused `amount` to the sender, leaving balances effectively unchanged; the function still returns true without reverting for valid senders.
Change the return value from true to false while keeping the transfer effect the same.
Replace the body of approve to return false instead of true after approving.
Delete the return statement in approve so no value is explicitly returned.
Replace the allowance update with a no-op so increaseAllowance returns true without changing the stored allowance.
Replace the successful return value with false so increaseAllowance returns a different value while still completing.
Change the require condition from currentAllowance >= subtractedValue to currentAllowance > subtractedValue, so exact allowance decreases revert instead of succeeding.
Change the subtraction in _approve from currentAllowance - subtractedValue to currentAllowance + subtractedValue.
Change the final return from true to false.
Delete the require guard so that underflow in currentAllowance - subtractedValue reverts with a panic instead of the guard's custom error message for insufficient allowance.

Changed the underflow guard require condition from currentAllowance >= subtractedValue to currentAllowance > subtractedValue, making decreaseAllowance revert when subtracting exactly the full allowance.
Deleted the guard require(currentAllowance >= subtractedValue, "!approval") so that an underflow on subtraction reverts with a Panic error instead of the custom "!approval" message.
Moved the state update _approve(...) before the require guard, so _allowances is updated before the allowance check executes.
Changed the approval update to add subtractedValue instead of subtracting it, increasing the allowance rather than decreasing it.
Replace `_transfer(sender, recipient, amount);` with a no-op expression, so transferFrom no longer moves tokens but still returns true.
Weaken the allowance check by changing `require(currentAllowance >= amount, "!approval")` to `require(currentAllowance >= 0, "!approval")`, allowing transfers above allowance to complete.
Change the approval decrement from `currentAllowance - amount` to `currentAllowance + amount`, so the spender's allowance increases after transferFrom.
Change the return statement from `return true;` to `return false;`, observing a different return value for a successful transferFrom.
Move the `require(currentAllowance >= amount, "!approval")` check from before the `_approve` update to after it.
